p.src: Now, although Lu Junyi was a formidable man, he could not swim. Zhang Shun, the White Streak in the Waves, overturned his boat and pitched him headlong into the water. Zhang Shun seized him around the waist underwater, swam with him to the opposite bank, and took away his long-handled saber. Zhang Shun carried Lu Junyi straight toward the shore. Torches had already been lit, and fifty or sixty men were waiting there. They received him ashore, surrounded him, removed the saber at his waist, stripped off all his wet clothes, and were about to bind him with rope. Just then Dai Zong, the Magic Messenger, relayed an order, shouting as he approached, “You must not harm the honorable person of Master Lu!” He immediately ordered someone to bring a bundle of brocade clothes and an embroidered coat for Lu Junyi to put on. Eight young followers carried over a sedan chair, helped Master Lu into it, and set off. In the distance, twenty or thirty pairs of red gauze lanterns could already be seen illuminating a company of horsemen, who approached to the sound of drums and music to welcome him. At their head were Song Jiang, Wu Yong, and Gongsun Sheng, followed by all the other chiefs, who dismounted together. Lu Junyi hurriedly descended from the sedan chair. Song Jiang knelt first, and all the chiefs behind him knelt in rows. Lu Junyi also knelt to return their courtesy and said, “Now that I have been captured, I beg only for a swift death!” Song Jiang laughed heartily and said, “For now, Master Lu, please return to the sedan chair.” The others all mounted, and, with drums and music playing, escorted him through the three passes, dismounting before the Hall of Loyalty and Righteousness. They invited Lu Junyi into the hall, where lamps and candles burned brilliantly. Song Jiang stepped forward and spoke courteously: “For a long time, this humble man has heard of your great name, Master Lu; it has rung in my ears like thunder. Today I have had the good fortune to meet and pay my respects to you, fulfilling one of my lifelong wishes. My brothers behaved most offensively just now; I earnestly beg your forgiveness.” Wu Yong stepped forward and said, “Acting on our elder brother’s order, I went personally to your residence on the pretext of telling fortunes, intending to bring you up the mountain so that we might unite in the great cause and together carry out Heaven’s justice.” Song Jiang then invited Master Lu to take the foremost seat. Lu Junyi returned the courtesy and replied, “I am an ignorant, incapable man who unwittingly offended your tigerish might. Even ten thousand deaths would be too light a punishment; why do you mock me so?” Song Jiang replied with a conciliatory smile, “How would I dare mock you? In truth, I admire your might and virtue as intensely as a starving man craves food or a thirsty man water. I earnestly hope you will not disdain this humble place but become master of our stronghold, so that morning and evening we may all obey your strict commands.” Lu Junyi answered, “I would sooner die; I truly cannot obey your request.” Wu Yong said, “We shall discuss it again tomorrow.” Food and wine were then prepared for his entertainment. Lu Junyi had no way out and could only drink a few cups. The young followers then conducted him to the rear hall to rest.

p.src: The next day, Song Jiang had sheep and horses slaughtered and laid out a magnificent banquet. Master Lu was invited to the feast and, after repeated exchanges of courtesy, was seated in the middle. After several rounds of wine, Song Jiang rose, offered him a cup, and said courteously, “Last night we treated you most rudely; I hope you will graciously forgive us. Though our stronghold is cramped and unworthy even to stable your horse, I ask that you consider the words ‘Loyalty and Righteousness.’ I, Song Jiang, willingly yield my position to you, so please do not refuse.” Lu Junyi replied, “You are mistaken, Chief! I am guilty of no crime and possess a modest estate of my own. Alive, I am a subject of the Great Song; dead, I shall be a ghost of the Great Song. I would sooner die than comply.” Wu Yong and every one of the chiefs tried to persuade him, but Lu Junyi grew only more determined not to become an outlaw. Wu Yong said, “Since you are unwilling, Master Lu, how could we force you? We might keep your person here, but we could not keep your heart. It is merely that our brothers have seldom had the honor of your presence. Since you will not join us, please stay a few days in our humble stronghold, and then we shall escort you home.” Lu Junyi said, “I do not mind staying here, but I fear my household knows nothing of what has happened.” Wu Yong said, “That is easily settled. We shall have Li Gu take the carts and baggage home first. What harm can there be if you return a few days later?” Wu Yong asked, “Steward Li, are all your carts and goods accounted for?” Li Gu replied, “Not the least thing is missing.” Song Jiang ordered two large ingots of silver brought for Li Gu, gave two smaller ingots to the attendants, and a total of ten taels of silver to the ten cart drivers. They all bowed in gratitude. Lu Junyi instructed Li Gu, “You know all about the hardship I have suffered. When you return home, tell my wife not to worry. I shall be back in three or five days.” Li Gu desired only to escape and readily promised, “There will be no problem at all.” He took his leave and went down from the Hall of Loyalty and Righteousness. Wu Yong immediately rose and said, “Rest easy and remain seated, Master Lu. I shall see Steward Li off down the mountain and return at once.”

p.src: On the pretext of seeing Li Gu off, Wu Yong went ahead to wait at Golden Sands Beach. A short while later, Li Gu, the two attendants, and all the carts, pack animals, and men came down the mountain. Wu Yong had five hundred young followers line both sides. Seated beneath the shade of a willow, he summoned Li Gu forward and said, “Your master has reached an agreement with us and now occupies the second seat of honor. Before coming up the mountain, he wrote four rebellious lines of verse on a wall in his home. Let me explain it to you: among the twenty-eight characters on the wall, each line conceals one character. ‘A single skiff amid the reed-flowered marsh’ conceals the character ‘Lu.’ ‘How could a hero wander in this place?’ conceals the character ‘Jun.’ ‘A righteous knight holds a three-foot sword’ conceals the character ‘Yi.’ ‘When rebellion comes, the traitorous minister’s head must be struck off’ conceals the character ‘rebel.’ These four lines conceal the four characters ‘Lu Junyi rebels.’ How could you know that he would come up the mountain today? We originally meant to kill all of you, but that would make it seem that we of Liangshan Marsh conduct ourselves dishonorably. Today we release you to hurry home through the night, but do not dream that your master will ever return!” Li Gu and the others did nothing but bow repeatedly. Wu Yong ordered a boat to carry them across to the landing. The party took to the road and hurried back to Beijing. Indeed: The giant turtle slips free of the golden hook, and, wagging head and tail, never returns.

He returned to the Hall of Loyalty and Righteousness, rejoined the banquet, and used artful words to entice Lu Junyi. The feast did not end until the second watch of the night. Tomorrow I, Song Jiang, shall personally prepare a modest drink, so that we may sit face-to-face and speak from the heart. Please do not refuse.” And so another day passed. The next day Song Jiang entertained him, the day after that Wu Yong, and the following day Gongsun Sheng. To avoid a tedious account: each of the more than thirty chiefs who attended the main hall took a turn hosting a banquet every day. p.src: The next day, Song Jiang once again privately prepared to see him off, but all the chieftains said, “Our elder brother shows Master Lu ten parts respect; we should show him twelve! Why should he attend only our elder brother’s banquet? ‘How can the brick be thick and the tile thin?’” Li Kui shouted from among them, “I risked my life and went straight to Beijing to bring you here. If you refuse to attend our brothers’ banquets, I’ll lock horns with you and fight you to the death!” Scholar Wu laughed heartily. “I have never seen anyone invite a guest in such a fashion. How very crude! Please do not take offense, Master Lu. In consideration of their humble goodwill, stay a few more days.” Before he knew it, another four or five days had passed, but Lu Junyi remained determined to leave. Then Zhu Wu, the Divine Strategist, led another group of chieftains straight into the Hall of Loyalty and Righteousness and said, “Though we brothers rank below the others, we too have labored for our elder brother. Can it be that poison is hidden only in our wine? If Master Lu takes offense and refuses to drink with us, I myself do not mind, but I fear the younger brothers may cause trouble, and then regret will come too late.” Wu Yong rose at once and said, “Do not fret. I shall plead with Master Lu on your behalf and ask him to stay a few more days. Why should he not? As the saying goes, ‘One who presses wine upon another can mean no harm in the end.’” Unable to withstand their insistence, Lu Junyi had no choice but to remain several more days. —All told, he had stayed a full fifty days. p.src: We shall say no more of Song Jiang’s return to the stronghold, but speak instead of Lu Junyi, who lengthened his stride and traveled by day and night. After ten days, he reached Beijing. It was already dusk, and he could not enter the city in time, so he spent the night at an inn. Early the next morning, Lu Junyi left the village inn and hurried into the city. With a little more than a li still to go, he saw a man in a tattered headcloth and ragged clothes, who bowed to the ground as soon as he caught sight of Lu Junyi. Lu Junyi looked closely and saw that it was Yan Qing, the Prodigal. He asked, “Xiao Yi, how did you come to look like this?” Yan Qing said, “This is no place to talk.” Lu Junyi went around to the side of an earthen wall and questioned him closely about what had happened. Yan Qing said, “Less than half a month after you left, Master, Li Gu returned and told the mistress, ‘The master has submitted to Song Jiang at Liangshan Marsh and taken the second-ranking seat.’ He went straight to the authorities and lodged an accusation. He had already joined forces with the mistress, and on the pretext that Yan Qing was disobedient, they drove me from the house. They stripped me of all my clothes and possessions and drove me outside the city. Moreover, he warned every relative and acquaintance that if anyone gave Yan Qing shelter in his home, he would spend half his fortune prosecuting that person. Thus no one dared take Xiao Yi in. Unable to find shelter in the city, I had no choice but to beg for a living outside the walls, and for now I am lodging in a hermitage. I was just about to go to Liangshan Marsh to seek you out, Master, but I dared not act rashly. If you have indeed come from the marsh, Master, please heed Xiao Yi’s words, return to Liangshan Marsh, and devise another plan. If you enter the city, you are certain to fall into their trap.” Lu Junyi shouted, “My wife is not that sort of woman! Stop farting nonsense, you wretch!” Yan Qing said again, “You have no eyes in the back of your head, Master. How could you know what has truly been happening? You have always cared only for training your strength and have never concerned yourself with women. The mistress and Li Gu had long been conducting an affair. Now that the way lies open, they have come together as husband and wife. If you go there, Master, you will surely meet a murderous end!” Lu Junyi flew into a rage and cursed Yan Qing, shouting, “My family has lived in Beijing for five generations. Who here does not know us? How many heads does Li Gu imagine he has, that he would dare commit such deeds? Perhaps it was you who committed some villainy, and now you have come to turn the accusation against others! Once I get home and learn the truth, I shall certainly not let you off!” Yan Qing wept bitterly, fell to his knees, and clutched at his master’s clothes. Lu Junyi kicked Yan Qing to the ground and strode into the city.

p.src: He hurried into the city and went straight home, where all the stewards, high and low, were startled at the sight of him. Li Gu hastened forward to welcome him, invited him into the hall, and immediately bowed his head to the floor. Lu Junyi asked at once, “Where is Yan Qing?” Li Gu replied, “Master, please do not ask what happened just yet. It is a long story! I fear you will grow angry; let me tell you after you have rested and composed yourself.” Madam Jia came out from behind the screen, weeping. Lu Junyi said, “My lady, do not weep. Just tell me what has happened to Little Yi, Yan Qing.” Madam Jia said, “Husband, please do not ask yet. I shall tell you everything presently.” Lu Junyi grew suspicious and uneasy and insisted on learning what had become of Yan Qing. Li Gu said, “Master, please change your clothes and take breakfast first. There will be ample time to explain afterward.” Meanwhile, a meal was prepared for Master Lu. He had only just lifted his chopsticks when shouts rose at both the front and rear gates, and two or three hundred constables burst inside. Lu Junyi was struck dumb with shock. The constables bound him and, beating him at every step, drove him straight to the governor's office. At that moment, Grand Secretary Liang was seated in the public court. In two ranks on either side stood seventy or eighty fierce constables, savage as wolves and tigers, and Lu Junyi was brought before him. Madam Jia and Li Gu were also kneeling to one side. From the bench Grand Secretary Liang thundered, “You are a respectable citizen native to this prefecture of Beijing. How dared you go over to the outlaws of Liangshan Marsh and take the second seat among them? And now you have returned to conspire from within with your confederates outside and attack Beijing! Now that you have been captured, what can you possibly say in your defense?” Lu Junyi said, “In a moment of folly, I was deceived by Wu Yong of Liangshan Marsh, who came to my house disguised as a fortune-teller, uttered false prophecies, and beguiled my honest mind. He tricked me into going to Liangshan Marsh, where I was kept under lenient confinement for more than two months. Today, by good fortune, I escaped and returned home. I harbor no evil intent whatsoever. I beg Your Excellency to discern the truth as clearly as a bright mirror.” Grand Secretary Liang shouted, “How can such a story hold water? If you had not been in league with the men of Liangshan Marsh, how could you have remained there so long? Your own wife and Li Gu have formally accused and denounced you. How can the charge be false?” Li Gu said, “Master, now that you have come here, you had better confess. The acrostic poem of rebellion written on the wall of the house remains as irrefutable evidence. There is no need to say more.” Madam Jia said, “It is not that we wish to harm you; I only fear that you will implicate me. As the saying goes, ‘When one man rebels, all nine degrees of his kin are put to death!’” Kneeling below the court, Lu Junyi cried out that he had been wronged. Li Gu said, “Master, there is no use protesting your innocence. Truth cannot be effaced, while falsehood is easily dispelled. p.src: That day autumn rain fell steadily, and the road was slippery. Lu Junyi stumbled at every step. Xue Ba raised his constable’s staff and struck him across the waist. Dong Chao pretended to restrain him, all the while grumbling and complaining as they went. After leaving the village inn and traveling another ten li or so, they reached a great wood. Lu Junyi said, “I truly can go no farther. Have pity and let me rest a while!” The two constables led him into the wood. Dawn was only just breaking in the east, and no travelers were about. Xue Ba said, “We two rose early and are terribly weary. We would like to sleep awhile here in the wood, but we fear you might run away.” Lu Junyi said, “Even if I grew wings, I could not fly away.” Xue Ba said, “We will not fall for any trick of yours. Let your masters bind you first.” He untied a hemp rope from his waist, looped it around Lu Junyi’s belly, pulled him tight against a pine, dragged his feet backward, and bound him to the tree. Xue Ba said to Dong Chao, “Elder brother, stand outside the wood. If anyone happens along, cough as a signal.” Dong Chao said, “Brother, be quick about it.” Xue Ba said, “Do not worry. Go and keep watch outside.” With that, he raised his constable’s staff, looked at Master Lu, and said, “Do not blame us two. Your steward Li Gu ordered us to finish you off on the road. Even if you reached Shamen Island, you would die there anyway. Better that we send you on your way now! When you reach the courts of the underworld, do not bear us a grudge. This day next year will be the anniversary of your death.” When Lu Junyi heard this, tears poured down like rain. He lowered his head and awaited death. Gripping the constable’s staff in both hands, Xue Ba brought it down toward the crown of Master Lu’s head. Outside the wood, Dong Chao heard a sudden thud. He rushed in to look and saw Master Lu still bound to the tree, while Xue Ba lay flat on his back beneath it, his constable’s staff cast aside. Dong Chao said, “What strange business is this! Can he have swung so hard that he fell over backward?” He raised his face and looked all around, but saw no movement. Blood flowed from Xue Ba’s mouth, and three or four inches of a slender arrow shaft protruded from the pit of his chest. Just as Dong Chao was about to cry out, he saw a man sitting in a tree at the northeastern corner and heard him shout, “Take that!” At the twang of the released bowstring, an arrow had already struck Dong Chao in the neck. His feet kicked the air, and he too fell to the ground with a thud.

Notices describing the two men were posted everywhere, and villages, inns, markets, towns, and households throughout the region were alerted and searched so that the fugitives might be seized. Meanwhile, Lu Junyi was recuperating from the wounds of his beating in a room at the village inn. Since he still could not walk, he had no choice but to remain there for the time being. The inn boy heard that there had been a murder. The local patrol chief came through the village, describing the appearance of the two wanted men. When the boy saw it, he hurried to report to the local community head: “There are two men at my inn who look extremely suspicious. p.src: The two approaching men happened to brush shoulders with Yan Qing. Yan Qing turned and looked at them, thinking, “I have no money for the journey. Why not knock the pair down with two blows, seize their bundle, and make my way to Liangshan Marsh?” He tucked away his crossbow and doubled back. The two men merely kept their heads lowered and walked on. Yan Qing caught up and punched the man behind, who wore a felt hat, squarely between the shoulders, knocking him sprawling to the ground. Just as he drew back his fist to strike the man in front, that fellow swung his staff down and caught Yan Qing squarely on the left leg, sending him tumbling. The man behind scrambled up, planted a foot on Yan Qing, drew the saber at his waist, and made to hack him full in the face. Yan Qing cried out, “Good sir, I do not mind dying—but then who will carry word for my master?” The man stayed his blade, drew back his hand, hauled Yan Qing up, and demanded, “What news are you carrying, you rogue?” Yan Qing said, “Why do you want to know?” The hero in front seized Yan Qing by the hand, exposing the flower tattoos on his wrist, and hurriedly asked, “Are you not ‘the Prodigal’ Yan Qing from Squire Lu’s household?” Yan Qing thought, “Either way I am dead. I may as well tell them and let them take me away, so that my ghost may join my master’s!” So he said, “I am indeed ‘the Prodigal’ Yan Qing of Squire Lu’s household. I am now bound for Liangshan Marsh to carry word and ask Song Gongming to save my master.” Hearing this, the two men roared with laughter and said, “Thank heaven we did not kill you! So you truly are Brother Yan Xiao’yi! Do you recognize the two of us?” The man in black was none other than Yang Xiong, the Liangshan chief known as “Sick Guan Suo”; the man behind was Shi Xiu, “the Desperate Third Son.” Yang Xiong said, “The two of us have come under our elder brother’s orders to Daming Prefecture to learn news of Squire Lu. The Strategist and Warden Dai have also descended from the mountain behind us and are waiting especially for our report.” When Yan Qing learned that they were Yang Xiong and Shi Xiu, he told them everything that had happened. Yang Xiong said, “Since matters stand thus, Yan Qing and I will return to the stronghold, inform our elder brother, and devise another plan. You go on alone to Daming Prefecture, learn what you can, and return at once to report.” Shi Xiu said, “That is best.” They gave the bundle to Yan Qing to carry, and he followed Yang Xiong through the night back to Liangshan Marsh. Once before Song Jiang, Yan Qing related the whole affair in full detail. Song Jiang was greatly alarmed and immediately gathered all the chiefs to discuss a sound plan.

u.src: Now Shi Xiu, carrying only the clothes he wore, reached the outskirts of Daming Prefecture after nightfall. Unable to enter the city, he spent the night outside its walls.
The next morning, after breakfast, he entered the city and saw everyone sighing in sorrow and grieving.
Shi Xiu grew suspicious.

When he reached the heart of the marketplace, he saw every household barred and shuttered. Shi Xiu questioned one of the townspeople, and an old man replied, “Traveler, you may not know that here in Daming Prefecture we have a great landowner named Squire Lu.

He was abducted by the bandits of Liangshan Marsh, and though he escaped and returned, he was then unjustly prosecuted and sentenced to exile on Shamen Island. Somehow or other, two constables were killed along the way.
He was brought back last night, and today at the third quarter of noon he will be escorted here to the execution ground and beheaded. You may watch if you wish.”

More than a dozen pairs of executioners armed with blades and staves crowded before and behind as Lu Junyi, bound and under guard, was brought to kneel before the winehouse. Cai Fu, “the Iron Arm,” held the executioner’s blade. Cai Qing, “A Flower,” supported the end of the cangue and said, “Squire Lu, look carefully for yourself. It is not that we brothers would not save you; the affair was badly managed. In the Temple of the Five Sages ahead, I have already prepared a seat for you. Let your soul go there and take possession of it.” As he finished speaking, someone in the crowd cried, “The third quarter of noon has arrived!” As the cangue was opened, Cai Qing promptly seized Lu’s head, while Cai Fu had already drawn the executioner’s blade. The clerk in charge of the case loudly finished reading the placard of crimes, and the crowd answered with one united shout. At that very shout, Shi Xiu upstairs whipped out his waist saber and cried in answer, “All the heroes of Liangshan Marsh are here!” Cai Fu and Cai Qing abandoned Squire Lu, tugged away the ropes, and fled first. Shi Xiu leapt down from the upper story, brandishing his steel saber. He cut men down as easily as slicing melons and chopping vegetables, killing more than a dozen who failed to escape in time. With one hand he seized Lu Junyi and fled southward.

p.src: But Shi Xiu did not know the streets of Daming Prefecture, while Squire Lu was so stunned with fright that he could scarcely walk. When Grand Secretary Liang received the report, he was greatly alarmed. He immediately mustered the officers under his command, sent troops out by separate routes, and had all four city gates closed. He ordered constables from every quarter to close in upon them. Hero and champion though you may be, how can you escape those lofty walls and towering ramparts? Indeed, to cleave open the earth they lacked fangs and claws; to soar into the blue heavens they lacked feathers and wings. How Squire Lu and Shi Xiu managed to escape will be revealed in the next chapter.
